name: zeek_run
description: Run the installed Zeek over a capture and read its logs back as records, with what ran recorded: the Zeek version as printed, the command, whether checksums were validated (-C is passed unless checksum_validation is true), and a policy script the tool writes into out_dir (by default one that loads policy/frameworks/files/hash-all-files; `policies` changes the list, an empty list loads nothing; a policy is a name Zeek resolves, never a path or a script from the evidence) with its path and SHA-256. Whether the installed build has a policy by that name, and which hash functions it computes, is not assumed: hashes_produced says whether any files.log record carries a hash value (hash_fields only names the columns, which a real install can have whether or not they were filled). The reader follows each log's own header (#separator, #set_separator, #empty_field, #unset_field, #fields, #types), \xNN escapes, sets and vectors as lists, typed numbers, and every time as raw text with a decoded `_utc` beside it; JSON logs are read too. A record that does not fit (a wrong column count, a value that is not its type, bad JSON or JSON nested deeper than 64 levels, no header, an empty or longer-than-8-character separator, empty-field or unset-field marker) is counted with its line and byte offset and kept whole in malformed-<log>.jsonl, and ok is false. Requested logs Zeek did not write are listed apart from logs written with no records; reporter, weird and capture_loss are always summarised (capture_loss exists only if its policy is loaded, so its absence is not a finding). conn.log rows are Zeek connections as Zeek defines them, not application data delivered. Every log stays whole in out_dir, named, and inline records are bounded by limit. SENSITIVE: logs can carry credentials, cookies and request URIs. The directory is private (0700/0600); inline records withhold secret-named fields and the hash of an object under 128 bytes, redact URLs, and scrub every other string except the typed kinds that are decided per log: Zeek's own identifiers (uid, fuid and the like), hashes and fingerprints, IP addresses in address fields, times, numbers, conn.log's service, conn_state and history (kerberos.log's service is a name from the wire and is scrubbed); a URL's host goes through the same rule as every other string (a token in a sub-domain is withheld), and so do the names under engine_diagnostics.weird.by_name (by shape: a short secret in free text is not recognised); run it as a job with secret_output: true. Zeek runs in the tool's own process group (the harness ending the tool ends Zeek; SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP kill it), and timeout_seconds is held under the manifest's limit. A failing `zeek --version` makes the run not ok. Every answer carries status (complete when Zeek exited 0, every log was read through and every line fit its header; partial otherwise; failed for a refusal) and status_basis; exit 0 means the engine ran and the answer says whether it was whole, and a refusal is JSON and exit 1. SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP kill Zeek and what it started, print partial JSON (the stage and the logs on disk) and exit 128 plus the signal. The names of the log files Zeek wrote are printed as Zeek chose them (the tool trusts the engine for them; a name chosen by the wire, which Zeek's own logs do not do, would be printed). A reporter message over 500 characters is shown cut with the count not shown and a pointer to reporter.log, where the whole is. The manifest declares secret_output: "required", so every job of this tool is run and sealed as secret output (the answer says so, secret_output_by: tool_manifest, and the process gets SECRET_OUTPUT=1).

out_dir.description: An empty directory under work/ (in a job, under $OUT; work/<your id>/name is mapped to $OUT/name) where Zeek runs and its logs land. It is private (0700, files 0600)

logs.description: Which logs to return inline, e.g. ["conn","dns","ssl"] (default: every log written). A name Zeek did not write is listed in logs_requested_not_written; reporter, weird and capture_loss are summarised regardless

limit.description: Maximum records per log returned inline (default 200); the whole log is the file named in its entry, and omitted says how many were not returned

timeout_seconds.description: Kill Zeek, and everything it started, after this long (10 to 1100 seconds, default 900), so that this tool stops Zeek before the 1200-second limit does

policies.description: Zeek policy names to load through the script the tool writes (default ["policy/frameworks/files/hash-all-files"]; [] loads none). Names only: a path, a name that climbs out of Zeek's script path or one under inputs/ is refused

checksum_validation.description: Leave Zeek's checksum validation on (default false: -C is passed, and the answer says checksums were not validated)
